# Training as a System {#sec-eng-training}

A training run is a long, expensive, failure-prone distributed job. This
chapter treats it as infrastructure: data moving reliably to compute,
checkpoints you can trust, and a run that survives the hardware it sits on.

By the end you will be able to lay out a training pipeline, choose a
parallelism strategy for a given model and cluster, and make a run
resumable and reproducible.

## The training pipeline

From raw data to a checkpoint: ingestion, preprocessing, sharding, and the
handoff to the training loop.

## Data infrastructure

Throughput from storage to accelerator, sharded and streaming datasets,
deduplication, and keeping the input pipeline from starving the hardware.

## Distributed training

Data, tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism, what each costs in
communication, and how to combine them for a model that does not fit on one
device.

## Checkpointing and fault tolerance

Asynchronous checkpoints, resuming exactly, elastic training across a
changing node count, and detecting a silently diverging run.

## Reproducibility and provenance

Pinning data, code, and configuration so a result can be regenerated, and
tracking the lineage from dataset to checkpoint.

## Cost and scheduling

Spot and preemptible capacity, gang scheduling, and the economics of a run
that occupies a cluster for days.
